I am 61, only finished primary school, and I have only been doing this for 2 years on my own. Before that I was doing other work. My wife and son help sometimes but my son works in town most of the year, so it is mostly me on these 7.7 mu. I cannot afford to lose a harvest — if the maize or wheat fails, that is real money gone.

I do what my neighbors do. Around here everyone plants wheat in October and maize in June, same land, two crops a year. I buy seed from the dealer in town — he sells the improved wheat seed that my neighbor Old Zhang uses, and the hybrid maize seed (the bag with the good picture, the one most people plant). Traditional seed nobody plants anymore, yield is too low.

For fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, and urea for topdressing. My neighbor told me: for wheat, put 2 bags of compound (one bag is 50 jin, 25 kg) per mu before planting, then topdress with urea in spring when the wheat greens up, about 20-25 kg per mu. For maize, same idea — one bag compound at planting, then urea at big trumpet stage, maybe 25 kg. I would rather put a little extra than too little. Fertilizer costs money but a bad harvest costs more.

Water — I have well irrigation, lucky. Wheat needs water in winter (before freezing), then spring jointing, then filling. That is 3 times usually. Maize is summer rain season so maybe 1-2 times if dry. If the rain comes good, less.

Pesticide I spray when I see bugs or when neighbors spray. For wheat, aphids in spring, maybe 1-2 times. For maize, corn borer, 1-2 times. I do not spray for nothing.

Tillage — I hire the rotary tiller from the village, everyone does. Plough is too much work, no-till I do not understand.

Yield — last year wheat was about 450 kg/mu, maize about 550 kg/mu. I hope for the same or a little better.
